first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both currently declining, making a targeted onboarding simplification the most direct response and one that may improve time-to-value without immediately discounting revenue. Verify memory_86 because it is the closest evidence for this intervention. Run a guarded test with qualification, conversion, retention, and revenue-quality guardrails so completion gains do not mask lower-value accounts. Promotional pricing addresses competitor pressure but risks margin and sustainable revenue, while referral and enterprise-sales interventions are less responsive to the current broad activation problem.

final.rationale: Run a standard, segmented onboarding-simplification experiment this week. The verified source shows completion increased 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%, directly addressing both current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Preserve uncertainty by testing against the current flow and monitoring qualified activation, conversion, retention, expansion, and revenue quality—not completion alone. Avoid broad rollout until downstream account quality and revenue effects are confirmed.
